title: Technical Storekeeper
description:
Job Description

Job Summary

The Technical Storekeeper is responsible for handling and managing the receiving, storage, and processing of incoming and outgoing spare parts and technical supplies at one or more Carnival Corporation owned and operated global destination. This role supports the overall management of inventory levels, ensuring that all materials are accurately accounted for, properly stored, and readily available for technical teams as needed. The Technical Storekeeper monitors stock levels, maintains accurate records, coordinates with procurement for replenishment, and ensures compliance with company policies and safety standards. The position requires strong organizational skills, attention to detail, and the ability to work collaboratively with maintenance and technical staff to support smooth operational workflows.

  • Inventory Management and Record Keeping
  • Keep accurate records regarding stock counts, requirements, and reporting needs.
  • Review and issue a weekly inventory list of technical spares.
  • Update and maintain system records upon arrival of new parts and tools.
  • Label and maintain all tools, equipment, and spare parts.
  • Audit incoming materials for accurate paperwork and counts.
  • Confirm deliveries against invoices for accuracy of store count.
  • Monitor inventory levels to prevent shortages or overstock situations.
  • Track usage of spare parts to support maintenance planning and budgeting.
  • Ordering and Procurement Support
  • Place requests for all parts necessary for the storeroom for review and approval.
  • Assist with purchasing items and materials as needed.
  • Liaise with staff, management, and vendors to source supplies efficiently.
  • Coordinate with procurement teams to ensure timely delivery of parts.
  • Review vendor quotes and maintain records of supplier transactions.
  • Suggest alternatives for unavailable or discontinued parts.
  • Stores Organization and Receiving
  • Maintain stores in an organized and well-ordered manner.
  • Assist with unloading containers, sorting, counting, and receiving materials.
  • Ensure proper storage, handling, and labeling of all parts and tools.
  • Implement storage systems to maximize space and accessibility.
  • Conduct regular inspections to ensure cleanliness and orderliness of storerooms.
  • Follow safety protocols when handling heavy or hazardous materials.
  • Reporting, Compliance, and Other Duties
  • Create required reports related to inventory, usage, and discrepancies.
  • Uphold environmental policies and procedures in all store operations.
  • Document and report any damaged or defective parts to management.
  • Perform any other duties assigned by management.
  • Support cross-functional teams by providing required spare parts and technical materials.
  • Assist in audits and inspections as needed.

Knowledge, Skills & Abilities Needed

  • Ability to adhere to the companyâs standards regarding dress and appearance.
  • Ability to maintain confidentiality and data protection standards when handling vendor financial or business documents
  • Ability to work collaboratively in a team-oriented environment as necessary.
  • Strong organizational and time-management skills, with the ability to multitask effectively.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication and interpersonal skills.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite and familiarity with data entry and reporting tools.
  • Detail orientated with a proactive approach to problem solving.
  • Ability to multi-task and think critically
  • Problem-solving and decision-making abilities
  • Strong planning and coordination skills, especially in handling multiple priorities under tight deadlines.
  • Must be physically fit.
  • Ability to work in an outdoor environment as needed.
  • May need to stand for long periods of time.
  • May be requested to work a shift schedule while at any of the destinations.
  • Knowledge: Understanding of workplace policies and procedures / Familiarity with team collaboration tools and techniques.
  • Skills: Strong time management and organizational skills
  • Abilities: Ability to maintain reliable and consistent attendance / Capacity to be punctual and meet deadlines / Ability to collaborate effectively with colleagues and work as part of a team / Demonstrated professionalism in all interactions and tasks.

HESS Responsibilities

  • Adhere to all company policies, procedures, and guidelines related to health, safety, environmental protection, and security.
  • Take all necessary precautions, use personal protective equipment (PPE), safety devices, and tools correctly and consistently, as required by the nature of the work.
  • Promptly report any unsafe conditions, incidents, or environmental concerns to the appropriate supervisor or HESS representative.
  • Take reasonable care for your own health and safety, as well as that of colleagues and others who may be affected by your actions.
  • Actively participate in HESS trainings and initiatives that promote a safe, secure, and environmentally sustainable workplace.
  • Cooperate fully with company efforts to maintain compliance with legal and regulatory requirements.
  • Seek opportunities to improve safety and environmental performance in daily tasks.

Essential/Minimum Qualifications

  • High School Diploma or GED ; equivalent experience is required; additional education in Hospitality or a related field is a plus
  • Current Health Certificate

Essential Experience Required

  • A minimum of two (2) years relevant work experience in a technical role
  • Ability to lift at least 50 pounds.
  • Ability to create reports and documentation skills.
  • Analytical and Numerate Skills
  • Strong interpersonal, problem solving, conflict resolution and communication skills.
  • Proficient in English
  • Proficient in Microsoft Office
  • Working knowledge of: Swimming hazards; Beach Hazards; Pool hazards Lifeguard training techniques
  • First aid and Cardio-pulmonary Resuscitation (CPR)
  • Prolonged periods sitting at a desk and working on a computer.
  • Must be able to lift up to 15 pounds at times.
  • All island employees must be physically able to participate in emergency lifesaving procedures and drills. Full use/range of motion of arms and legs as well as full visual, verbal and hearing abilities are required to receive and give instructions in the event of an emergency.

during beta, yes â both tiers, no credit card, no trial clock. after beta: core is $10/machine/month for monitoring, control, deploy, displays, and cortex on a single site. pro is $50/machine/month (3-machine minimum) and adds the public API, CLI, SDK, webhooks, unlimited sites, and roost â incremental project sync with 1 TB included storage per site. no per-user fees on either.

no. owlette is windows-only. your mac is fine â it doesn't need monitoring. it'll let you know when something's wrong. loudly. in the middle of a show.

the agent keeps running. it monitors and auto-recovers processes whether or not it can reach the cloud. when the connection returns, it syncs everything it missed. your machines don't need the internet to run. they've been alone before. they know how to survive.

no inbound ports, no vpn. agents connect outbound over https (port 443) to google's firebase infrastructure. if your network allows general internet access, it just works. locked-down environments may need to whitelist *.googleapis.com and *.firebaseio.com.

cortex is owlette's ai fleet assistant â ask it the questions you ask yourself every day: "which nvidia driver are we running?", "restart the media server on node 3", "what crashed at 3am?" it translates natural language into real commands across your fleet. you bring your own api key (openai, anthropic, or any compatible provider).

roost is owlette's project sync. point it at a folder â a TouchDesigner project, a content drop, a build output â and it ships only the bytes that changed to every machine on the site, atomically: a machine gets the whole new version or stays on the old one, never a half-copied mess. every deploy is versioned, so you can roll back to any of the last 50 for up to 30 days. it's part of the pro tier and includes 1 TB of storage per site ($0.05/GB after that). no more zipping a folder and RDP-ing into ten machines at 2am.

agents connect over tls, credentials are encrypted on-device using a machine-bound key, and oauth tokens are never logged or stored in plaintext. access is managed through firebase auth with optional passkey and two-factor authentication.

yes â owlette is FSL-1.1-Apache-2.0 (converts to apache 2.0 two years after each release). the full source is on github. fair warning: it requires firebase, a railway (or equivalent) deployment for the web app, and a willingness to blow past your usage limits at 3am debugging support tickets from your neighbor's camper because your furnace broke and it's -10 outside. we won't talk you out of it, but the hosted version exists for a reason.

title: Donât Put Yourself a Box
description:
Photo by Piotr MusioÅ / Unsplash

Donât Put Yourself in a Box

Personal Development and Career Growth

  • Apr 26, 2024

Summary

  • Companies need "boxes" (job classifications) to grow and function. This makes hiring, compensation, and career development tractable, and promotes fair treatment of employees.
  • If the boxes are too large, a company can't grow. If the boxes are too small, innovation and ownership are smothered.
  • The size of a company's boxes is directly proportional to the level of trust employees have for management.
  • To get hired, put yourself in the box the company is hiring for. Tailor your resume to highlight those skills and experiences; put yourself out there as a âspecialistâ in the thing theyâre hiring for.
  • If aiming for a promotion, demonstrate how your work embodies the behaviors and impacts of the next-level âboxâ.
  • Don't let those boxes define you. Your value and identity goes far beyond any job description.

Hot Take

Businesses can't function at scale unless they put people in standardized "boxes"; if you want to be hired and to grow your career, you need to understand that, and understand how to work with those boxes. On the other hand, you can't be reduced to a box, and if you tie your identity to those boxes in your thinking, you'll limit yourself in ways that are unnatural and harmful.

This is like the paradox of SchrÃ¶dinger's Cat, both alive and dead at the same time. Like with quantum mechanics and the cat, whether youâre in a box or not depends on whoâs doing the measuring: your employer, or you.

My Box Origin Story

My introduction to the idea of âboxesâ came in the late 2000s, when I noticed that people at Google were having a hard time getting hired or promoted if they were doing âoperationalâ work that didnât involve much traditional program management. Whether they were being considered for hiring or promotion, they were told, essentially, âYouâve done some great work, but itâs not program management; weâre not sure what role/ladder is a fit for you, but itâs not this one. Next!â

This was clearly a problemâeven though they didnât do PERT diagrams and Gantt charts, Googlers did important work in these roles, and roadblocks to hiring and promoting them created both operational and retention issues as jobs went vacant and high-performing employees felt their value wasnât being recognized. As a member of both Program Management hiring and promotion committees at Google I had more visibility to this issue than most others; I spoke to a friend of mine in People Operations (Googleâs HR), who turned out to already be well aware of this problem from repeatedly dealing with upset hiring managers and frustrated promotion candidates. Together, we hatched a plan: to create a new job ladder (job classification) for these âoperationalâ program managers to move to, that was better suited to the type of work they did.

We gathered some data, wrote a proposal, and set up a meeting with the SVP responsible for all engineering at Google. The SVP had been in quite a few meetings Iâd presented to before; I knew him to be not only a brilliant and capable leader, but a genuinely nice guy, too, so I had no worries about the meeting. Imagine my shock then, when this âgenuinely nice guyâ started yelling at us, telling my partner and I that we were going to wreck Google culture!

I vividly remember what he said: âDONâT PUT PEOPLE IN BOXES!â He told us Google needed some job classifications, but that our culture required those classifications to be both broad and vague so both employees and their managers wouldnât be blocked from doing whatever needed to be done. The worst thing we could do, the SVP told us, was to make the classification âboxesâ so small people could say âthatâs not my jobââwhich is precisely what he saw us proposing to do!

A year or two before this Google had shifted from having just three job types (over-broadly, they were âengineersâ, âtechnical people that donât do engineeringâ, and âeveryone elseâ) to having around around a dozen (one of which was my ladder, âTechnical Program Managersâ). There had been a lot of debate about whether those boxes were already too smallâ¦ but the senior team had decided 12â15 job categories were acceptableâenough large boxes to make hiring, career development, and compensation more efficient, but not so many that jobs were defined too narrowly. We left his office dejected, but also enlightened: it said a lot to me that this SVP thought it so important to Googleâs culture, a lesson Iâve never forgotten. (Times have changed though; Google now has many more job ladders, including at least 5â10 âoperationalâ ladders broken off from Program Management well beyond what my friend and I had proposed).

Why Companies Need Boxes

Why do we need âboxesâ (job classifications) at all? Wouldnât the world be better if everyone just did whatever they saw that needed doing? The value of boxes to corporations comes down to two things: scaling and trust.

Scaling

If youâre in a small startup, you want employees who can wear many hats, and who wonât feel limited by things like job titles. Because there are so few employees, and because you know everyone personally and need everyone you hire to have an outsized impact, you can afford to put a lot of energy into every individual hiring decision. Compensation planning is pretty lightweight and customized, both because there arenât many people to deal with, and because you want to compensate people based on their contribution to the business, regardless of what their title is. Everyone is a âspecial snowflakeâ.

That changes quickly as your startup growsâyou cross a line where it becomes infeasible to treat every hire as a unique individual, with bespoke hiring and compensation. This is where âboxesâ become necessary: you have to put people into categories, with standards for how hiring, compensation, and career progression work for each boxâitâs the only way you can scale the company. The alternative to this would be to allow an increasing number of managers to continue bespoke hiring and comp within their own areasâ¦ which leads to the second issue, trust.

Trust

Because startups are so risky, the ability of potential employees to trust the founders is a big dealâif they donât appear trustworthy, theyâre not going to attract the kind of people they need. As the company grows, the number of managers that both employees and senior management need to trust grows, too. At some point it becomes too much: employeesâ willingness to âhave faithâ that managers will make fair and appropriate decisions drops lower and lower, so much so that everything will fall apart without the enforced fairness of standardized boxes.

ð¡

The size of the boxes in a company are directly proportional to the amount of trust employees have in management

Labor unions are the endgame for this sort of trust problem. One of the big rallying points for companies trying to avoid unionization is always to try to convince employees that management has their best interests at heart, and can be trusted. As a rule, unions have close to zero trust for management, andâas a direct consequenceâunions often push for the smallest âboxesâ possible: boxes for very narrow roles, subdivided by seniority, and sometimes further subdivided by location. They see this as the best way to ensure fairness in an environment where management canât be trusted at all. This is the ultimate version of the cultural harm my SVP was worried about.

Boxes and Hiring

Scaling and trust drive companies to put employees into standard categories, or boxes. How do those boxes affect hiring, and, understanding this, how can you better âsellâ yourself as a candidate for jobs?

Most companies above startup size need to hire for boxes, for the reasons given above; itâs just too much work to do anything else. It would be wonderful if recruiters, interviewers, and hiring managers had the time to carefully read and savor every resume that came in, and then spend time meeting with every candidate to pull out nuances that didnât come across clearly in their job histories. Thatâs not the world we live in, though; there are too many candidates to get through, and too few hours in the day.

The usual practice is for recruiters to work with hiring managers to identify standard requirements (boxes, again!) that can be used to screen out people and reduce the number of candidates they need to go into more depth with (hiring managers will usually never see any of those dropped candidates). Those standard requirements are typically based on a template used for all jobs of the same ladder and level, extended with custom specs tailored to the particular role being hired for. In the language Iâve been using in this article, the job requirements are a very clear âboxâ, and the screening process only lets through candidates whose âshapesâ fit that box, like a childâs sorting toy.

Source: Flickr user rosipaw, CC BY-NC-SA 2.0

When there are lots of candidates for a tiny number of jobs, the recruiters donât magically get more time to handle the extra candidatesâinstead, they often deal with the overload by tightening the screening criteria even further: that is, by making the boxes smaller.

Behaviorally, the shift from âstartupâ to âbig companyâ, and the shift from rapid growth to slow growth, show up to candidates as employers become increasingly selective. Startups like generalists; big companies like specialists. If there are few people vying for each job, hiring managers won't care as much about past experience; if there are many candidates, theyâll only be interested in people whoâve previously done the same kind job theyâre hiring for. These trends are amplified when business is tough and hiring budgets are thin: hiring managers become nervous about using their scarce headcount on unproven candidatesâthey need people who have already shown success in exactly the job the manager needs done.

ð¡

Iâm writing this in April, 2024, in a time of high interest rates and widespread layoffs in tech, and when there are lots of AI-based screening tools being offered that promise to save recruiters time; you do the math about the current hiring marketâ¦

Besides being lucky, there are two powerful ways to cut through âsmall box screeningâ:

  • Put yourself in the box theyâre hiring for. This means customizing your resume for each job you apply for, or at least for each type of job youâre going after. If theyâre hiring for someone with experience doing X, focus your resume on how youâve been successful doing X (or at least, things like X) in the past. When a recruiter or hiring manager looks at your resume, you want them to jump out of their chair and exclaim: âwow, this person is exactly what weâve been looking for!â
  • Pull a Kobayashi Maru by bypassing the whole screening process: use your network of personal connections to get an introduction to the hiring manager. This is probably the single most powerful thing you can do because it exposes you to the hiring manager as a whole person, instead of a peg that fits in a box.

Boxes and Promotions

A similar situation arises with promotions: the people making decisions about whether you should be promoted or not donât (usually) have the familiarity with you, or the time, to make a customized decisionâ¦ and doing so would create fairness issues. Instead, they look at whether you fit the next-level box. I want to talk about two parts to this: one related to the job ladder, and one related to the level.

Job Ladder

I vividly remember one promotion committee I served on, where we were deciding whether or not to promote an individual who had unquestionably performed at the next levelâ¦ but the work theyâd done wasnât consistent with the job ladder (work classification) they were assigned to. They had delivered amazing business impact through striking personal initiative, leadership, and hard workâ¦ but what theyâd done had nothing in common with the sort of work expected for the job ladder, or âboxâ, they were in. Should we promote them, or not? We debated the question for far longer than weâd spent on any other candidate weâd reviewed, called in HR support to advise us, andâ¦ we couldnât decide. The rules were that âif you canât decide, the decision needs to be ânoââ, so we ended by turning down the promotion and recommending the person for a large cash bonus, instead. Our decision was appealed, and the appeal was denied, too, for the same reason: despite the great work, the candidateâs work was outside the box.

Sometimes the process and people deciding on your promotions will be more amenable to âoutside the boxâ work, but really, regardless of whoâs making the promotion decision, and what their ârules of engagementâ are, your chances of success will be greatly enhanced by you being aware of the box imposed by your job ladder as you go about your work, and as you explain that work to others. To be clear: Iâm not saying to limit what you work onâthatâs the ânot my jobâ problem the SVP at the beginning of the article was talking about! What I am saying is that you should proactively plan how you will describe your work in ways consistent with the box.

For example, if youâre a Program Manager and spent a lot of time creating product requirements (the work of a Product Manager at most companies), when you and your direct manager describe it to others, be sure you both talk about (for example) the work you did to understand what other work was dependent on having the requirements, how you delegated and tracked some of the work on market research, bringing it all together into a single document, how you built consensus on the requirements, communicated them to the engineering team, and then managed scope creepâall things that are part of the description of the Program Management box. This makes it easy for the people who will decide on your promotion to say âHuzzah! They did both the Program and Product Managementâ, instead of saying âThis was great Product Management, too bad theyâre a Program Manager.â

Job Level

Really, this is a topic that deserves (and will get) an article all on its own, but I think itâs relevant to surface it here: in general, higher level jobs arenât just harder/bigger/broader versions of lower level jobs: theyâre different âboxesâ altogether. The next-level behaviors senior people are looking for are often behaviors that arenât exercised much, if at all, at your current level. I think of these as âphase changesâ, analogous to the phase changes water goes through as it turns from solid ice to liquid to gas as you turn up the heat: itâs always the same water, but it looks and behaves differently in each phase. Some of these transitions are more abrupt and noticeable than others, but theyâre definitely there. At Google for example, there are noticeable differences between all levels, but the âphase changesâ are especially acute between levels 5 and 6, and between levels 7 and 8.

The takeaway here is that you can greatly increases your chances of success by understanding what those âphase changesâ are (more senior mentors can be super helpful in this)âwhatâs qualitatively different about the next-level boxâand then work with your manager to proactively plan how you will describe your work in ways that highlight those qualitative differences.

Boxes and You

So after telling you about the importance of âboxesâ, now Iâm going to tell youâ¦ to avoid them!

This sure looks like a paradox, but let me explain!

Weâve been talking about how companies, managers, and recruiters use boxes, and how, because of scaling and trust, itâs just not practical for them to operate in any other way. Weâd hope that they donât make the boxes too small, and that they have good judgment in how they apply themâ¦ but boxes are a fact of life in the world of work.

The place where you should avoid boxes isnât in the workplace, though: it's in your head. Itâs completely natural for peopleâs occupation and organization to become a part of their identityâ¦ but it's harmful to let that go too far: you are not your job, and you are not your job title.

A lot has been written about the psychology of tying oneâs identity to their job, but the thing I want to focus on here is how putting yourself in a box in your own thinking (e.g. seeing yourself as a âProduct Managerâ, as a âGooglerâ, and so on) can mean putting counterproductive limits on your own behavior, and your own thinking about whatâs possible.

ð¡

Youâre much more than, and much more capable than, the box youâre in.

From a career perspective, itâs a good practice to periodically take some time out and take stock of where you are now and how that fits with where you want to go. If you do this sort of self-assessment youâll often decide youâre basically on the right path and just need to make some minor adjustmentsâ¦ but sometimes youâll realize that the path youâre on wonât take you where you want to be, and that bigger changes are needed: maybe you should ask your manager for different responsibilities? Change teams? Change job ladders? Even change companies? All of those require seeing beyond the box youâre in.

Even though you need to describe yourself in terms of boxes to get where you are now, if your own thinking is constrained by those boxes, it will be hard for you to see that maybe the best path for you is quite different from the one youâre on. Maybe you should change teams? Roles? Departments? Even change your city, or your employer? Donât get me wrong: I know plenty of people whoâve been in more or less the same job, in the same place, working for the same company, for many years, and theyâre very happyâ¦ but itâs also common for people stay in the same role because they see that role defining them, instead of just being something they do.

How You Can Bring Order From Chaos, Today

Here are some things you can do now to apply these ideas:

  • If youâre looking for a job now, describe yourself as being well inside the box your potential employer is hiring for: tune your resume to the job youâre going after. You should have a different resume at least for every âclassâ of job, and sometimes for each specific job. It can be hard to do it if youâre going after several types of job at the same time, but your LinkedIn resume needs to support the more focused, specialized resumes youâre using. Make sure you highlight the skills and expertise called out in the job ads youâre applying to, and talk about your skill and experience in that area. No one hires generalists, so donât call yourself one in your resume; instead, describe yourself as a specialist in the very thing your target company is hiring for.
  • If youâre working toward a promotion now, put yourself in the box you want to be promoted to. Ask your manager and mentors to help you understand the heart of the next-level box, and think about how you can describe your work, behavior, and accomplishments in terms of that box.
  • Donât tie your identity to the box youâre in. You are a complete person with a personality, skills, and experience that transcend any mere box, and if you tie up your identity with the boxes other people put you in, you will limit the paths you can take and the things you can accomplish.

What Do You Think?

I'd love to hear about your experiences with boxes! If you're a paid supporter of this newsletter (hint, hint!) you can add comments below.

title: Procurement Specialist
description:
We are looking for a detail-oriented Procurement Specialist to join our team in New York, New York in a contract capacity with the potential for a permanent role. This position will play an important role in supporting day-to-day purchasing operations, maintaining strong vendor documentation, and helping ensure procurement activities run smoothly across the business. The ideal candidate brings sound judgment, strong organizational skills, and the ability to coordinate effectively with suppliers, finance partners, and internal stakeholders in a fast-moving environment.

Responsibilities:
â¢ Manage the full processing cycle for purchase requests and purchase orders, ensuring accuracy, completeness, and timely execution.
â¢ Gather and evaluate vendor quotations for routine buying needs, helping identify competitive pricing and suitable supplier options.
â¢ Assist with supplier setup by collecting and organizing required forms, compliance records, insurance documents, and payment information.
â¢ Maintain current procurement records, including vendor profiles, contract files, and supporting purchasing documentation.
â¢ Monitor open orders, shipment timelines, and invoice-related issues, following up to resolve discrepancies efficiently.
â¢ Partner with Accounts Payable, Finance, and internal teams to address mismatches involving purchase orders, receipts, and invoices.
â¢ Track supplier agreement milestones and renewal timelines while helping maintain an organized contract and vendor calendar.
â¢ Prepare spend reports and purchasing analysis by supplier, category, and department to support business decision-making.
â¢ Help enforce procurement procedures by confirming purchases follow established approval steps and company policy requirements.
â¢ Contribute to sourcing activities by supporting bid reviews, supplier comparisons, reporting needs, audit documentation, and process improvement efforts within procurement systems and records management.
â¢ Bachelorâs degree in business, supply chain, accounting, or a related field, or equivalent relevant experience.
â¢ 1â3 years of experience in procurement, purchasing, accounts payable, vendor administration, or a related function.
â¢ Working knowledge of corporate procurement practices, purchase order processing, and buying workflows.
â¢ Exposure to vendor support activities, contract-related administration, or contract negotiation coordination is preferred.
â¢ Strong Excel skills and experience using purchasing platforms or enterprise procurement systems.
â¢ Excellent attention to detail with the ability to manage documentation, deadlines, and multiple priorities effectively.
â¢ Clear communication and sound problem-solving skills for working with suppliers and cross-functional internal teams.
â¢ Ability to perform well in a fast-paced environment that requires adaptability and strong follow-through.

description:
We are seeking a Senior Engineering Manager to join our 200+ product development organization and lead our Ad Performance Recommendation team. The team is responsible for developing an innovative AI-powered system that leverages marketing ad tech data and various data sources to identify performance signals and generate actionable recommendations for digital advertisers and marketers. 

As part of the AI Platform organization, you will lead a multidisciplinary team of Data Scientists, ML Engineers, and Software Engineers working to accelerate AI adoption and development across Smartly's Media, Creative, and Intelligence suite. The team ensures compliance with privacy, security, and ethical guidelines.

This is an opportunity to define the vision and strategy for ML and Data Science applications, drive execution on ambitious goals, and champion AI and ML excellence throughout Smartly.

Smartly is proud to be ranked as a leader in The Forrester Wave™ for Creative AdTech. This recognition reflects our commitment to transforming ad experiences through intelligent creativity, standing as the only platform honored by both Forrester and validated by PwC to be recognized for ad technology to power performance.

To get an idea of some of the work we do, see for example these blog posts:

How We Productized Bayesian Revenue Estimation with Stan

Optimizing Conversions with Predictive Budget Allocation

title: Senior Analytics Engineer, Consumer
description:

The role is focused on the business needs - you'll be working within a cross-functional team, making sure your teammates get the insights needed for their operations. Data Scientists working in the domain will be your closest partners in your day-to-day work, as your solutions will enable them to create relevant experiments, A/B tests, and analyses.

What we offer

  • The online delivery platform that Wolt is building will offer you interesting and complex challenges, together with the opportunities to create a big impact with your skills. Lots of geolocational and temporal data in real-time, combined with differences in the economics and dynamics of the cities we operate in, make Wolt both a challenging and interesting company to practice analytics.

The position will be filled as soon as we find the right person, so make sure to apply as soon as you realize you really, really want to join us!

Must-have

  • Microsoft SQL Server
  • Hyper-V
  • IIS

Darüber hinaus freuen wir uns über Erfahrung mit einigen dieser Technologien:

Nice-to-have

  • Microsoft 365
  • Azure
  • Linux, insbesondere Debian oder Ubuntu
  • Docker
  • MongoDB
  • PostgreSQL

  • Kurze Wege

    Von Windows Server über Datenbanken und Virtualisierung bis zu Security und Cloud-Technologien erwartet dich ein breites technisches Umfeld.

    Du erhältst einen unbefristeten Arbeitsvertrag in einem inhabergeführten Unternehmen, in dem Zuverlässigkeit nicht nur auf der Website steht, sondern gelebt wird.

  • Ein Team, das zusammenarbeitet
    Dich erwartet ein Team, das sich gegenseitig unterstützt, Wissen teilt und gemeinsam Lösungen findet. Ehrlich gesagt finden wir sogar, dass es das beste Team aller Zeiten ist. Wahrscheinlich sagen das viele. Wir meinen es wirklich.

  • Ein Büro mit Charakter

title: Immobilienexperte
description:
Als Deutschlands am schnellsten wachsender digitaler Baufinanzierungsvermittler und Finanzberater, suchen wir Immobilienexpert:innen, die unser Team bei der Erfüllung unserer Mission, Menschen zu glücklichen Hausbesitzern zu machen, unterstützen.

Wir bilden ein motiviertes Team, das sich gegenseitig unterstützt, voneinander lernt und datenbasiert arbeitet. Unser Ziel ist es, durch den Einsatz modernster Technologien uns intensiv um unsere Kundinnen und Kunden zu kümmern und ihnen die besten Ergebnisse zu liefern. Dafür suchen wir Baufinanzierungsexpert:innen, die gemeinsam mit uns den Status quo verändern wollen.

Aufgaben

Deine Aufgaben

  • Du begleitest unsere Kund:innen durch den gesamten Immobilienkauf – von der Immobiliensuche bis zum erfolgreichen Notartermin und bist dabei eine vertrauenswürdige Ansprechperson für Deine Kund:innen.
  • Du bewertest Immobilien und führst Besichtigungen vor Ort durch, um Zustand, mögliche Risiken sowie anstehende Renovierungs- oder Modernisierungskosten einzuschätzen.
  • Du ermittelst den realistischen Marktwert von Immobilien anhand von Marktdaten, Vergleichsobjekten und unseren internen Tools und hilfst unseren Kund:innen so, fundierte Kaufentscheidungen zu treffen.
  • Du prüfst alle relevanten Objektunterlagen – z. B. Grundbuchauszüge, Teilungserklärungen, WEG-Unterlagen und Protokolle, Energieausweise oder Bauunterlagen – und identifizierst mögliche Risiken.
  • Du unterstützt unsere Kund:innen bei der Kaufpreisverhandlung und entwickelst auf Basis deiner Einschätzung und aktueller Marktdaten eine passende Verhandlungsstrategie.
  • Du koordinierst den Kaufprozess mit allen Beteiligten, darunter Verkäufer:innen, Makler:innen, Notar:innen, Finanzierungsexpert:innen und bei Bedarf weiteren externen Sachverständigen.
  • Du begleitest die Vorbereitung des Kaufvertrags und den Notarprozesses und stellst sicher, dass unsere Kund:innen die relevanten Inhalte und nächsten Schritte verstehen.
  • Du bringst deine Immobilienexpertise und das Feedback unserer Kund:innen ein, um Hypofriend Plus gemeinsam mit uns weiterzuentwickeln und unsere Prozesse und Services kontinuierlich zu verbessern.

Qualifikation

Danach suchen wir

  • Du lebst idealerweise bereits seit mehreren Jahren in Berlin, kennst den Berliner Immobilienmarkt wie Deine Westentasche – die verschiedenen Kieze, ihre Besonderheiten und kannst einschätzen, welche Lage zu welchen Bedürfnissen und Budgets passt.
  • Du bringst eigene praktische Erfahrung mit Immobilien mit – idealerweise hast du bereits selbst eine oder mehrere Immobilien gekauft und dich dabei auch mit Renovierung, Sanierung oder Modernisierung beschäftigt. Außerdem kannst Du mögliche Risiken oder versteckte Kosten einschätzen.
  • Du bist kommunikationsstark und gerne im direkten Austausch mit Kund:innen. Du kannst gut zuhören, verstehst schnell, was Menschen wirklich suchen, und schaffst es, Vertrauen aufzubauen.
  • Gleichzeitig scheust du dich nicht davor, ehrlich zu beraten und Erwartungen zu challengen – etwa wenn Budget, gewünschte Lage und Anforderungen nicht zusammenpassen – und zeigst konstruktiv Alternativen auf.
  • Du kannst dich gut in unterschiedliche Menschen und Lebenssituationen hineinversetzen und verstehst, dass der Kauf des eigenen Zuhauses eine emotionale Entscheidung ist, die trotzdem auf rationalen Fakten basieren sollte.
  • Du arbeitest eigenständig, strukturiert und lösungsorientiert und behältst auch bei mehreren parallelen Such- und Kaufprozessen den Überblick. Teamplay liegt Dir im Blut!
  • Vor allem hast du Lust darauf, Menschen dabei zu helfen, das Zuhause zu finden, das wirklich zu ihnen passt – und sie bei einer der wichtigsten Entscheidungen ihres Lebens kompetent und persönlich zu begleiten.

Benefits

👪 Team: Arbeite in einem jungen, motivierten und interdisziplinären Team, das bereits erfolgreich digitale Produkte entwickelt hat.

⏱️ Flexibilität: Flexible Arbeitsregelungen, inklusive der Möglichkeit, von zu Hause aus zu arbeiten (mit gelegentlichen Zusammenkünften im Berliner Office).

💰 Kompensation: Wir bieten ein sehr attraktives und wettbewerbsfähiges Gehaltspaket (mit einem zusätzlichen Bonus)

💻 Equipment: Wir bieten das neueste Macbook und ein Home Office Budget zur Optimierung deiner Produktivität.

🏃🏼‍♂️ Gesundheit: Neben einer kostenlosen Urban Sports Club-Mitgliedschaft bieten wir Dir im Büro Obst und Getränke.

📚 Lernen: Du bekommst Trainingstage, Online-Schulungstools sowie Coachings, um tiefe Einblicke in Investitionsberatung, Technologie und Marketing zu gewinnen.

🥳 Events: Wir organisieren regelmäßige Team-Events wie Hypofriend-BBQs, Happy-Hour mit unserem berühmten Pub Quiz oder Team Retreats, für das wir mit dem gesamten Team in die Natur fahren zum Workshoppen & strategischen Planen :)

description:
Als VC-backed Foodtech-Startup schaffen wir den Spagat zwischen gesunder Ernährung, Verfügbarkeit und Nachhaltigkeit. Mit unseren Foodjis bringen wir ultrafrische, leckere Gerichte genau dorthin wo du die meiste Zeit verbringst - denn wir haben uns zum Ziel gesetzt über 10 Millionen Arbeitnehmern endlich Zugang zu gesunder Ernährung zu ermöglichen und gleichzeitig Foodwaste zu reduzieren.

Als Werkstudent:in PR & Externe Kommunikation übernimmst du die komplette PR-Arbeit inhouse – von der Themenplanung über Journalist:innenkontakte bis zum Pressetext.

  • Beim Aufbau unserer PR inhouse bist du von Anfang an dabei: Themenplanung und Kernbotschaften entstehen gemeinsam mit dir.

DAS BRINGST DU MIT

Was für uns wirklich zählt: Mindset, Energie und der Wille, richtig gut zu werden – egal welchen Hintergrund du mitbringst. Alles andere bringen wir dir bei.

  • Eingeschriebene:r Student:in (z. B. Kommunikation, Medien, PR, Marketing, BWL)

  • Sehr gute Deutschkenntnisse und gutes Englisch in Wort und Schrift

  • Sicherer Schreibstil und Freude an präziser, zielgruppengerechter Kommunikation

  • Hands-on-Mindset und Teamspirit

  • Offenheit für neue Tools (z. B. Docs, Slides, Spreadsheets, LinkedIn)

DAS BIETEN WIR DIR

  • Office Foodji: Immer bestens versorgt bei uns im Office

  • Spendit Card: Wir stocken dein Gehalt auf! Mit Spendit stehen dir bis zu fünfzig Euro netto im Monat on top zur freien Verfügung

  • EGYM Wellpass: Mit uns bleibst du fit & wir bringen dich deutschlandweit in die angesagtesten Fitness- und Wellnessstudios

  • KITA/Kiga Kostenzuschuss: Wir bezuschussen deine Kosten für die Kinderbetreuung, damit deine Kinder immer bestens versorgt sind

  • Mitarbeiterrabatte: Du erhältst attraktive Promotions und Discounts verschiedener Brands

  • Food Tastings: Teste dich mit unserem Foodteam durch unsere Produkte und gestalte unser Sortiment von morgen

  • Development: Deine Weiterentwicklung liegt uns am Herzen und mit regelmäßigen Feedbackgesprächen und Trainings bieten wir dir spannende Perspektiven!

  • Top Office Lage: Genieße eine erstklassige Arbeitsumgebung im Münchener Glockenbachviertel mit der Isar vor der Tür

  • Team Events: Wir sind ein Team - beim Skiday, Frühstück, Culture Week oder Office Party feiern wir gemeinsam!

NOCH FRAGEN?

Silja freut sich auf deine Nachricht und hilft dir gerne weiter!

  • ÜBER UNS 

    Hi, schön, dass du da bist! Wir sind Foodji - ein Team aus Food-Lovern & Tech-Nerds.

    Unsere Mission ist es, frisches, gesundes und vor allem leckeres Essen überall dort anzubieten, wo Menschen den Großteil ihres Alltages verbringen - in Büros im Gewerbegebiet, wo es weit und breit nichts zu Essen gibt, in einer langen Schicht im Krankenhaus oder in den Tiefen einer Produktionshalle, in der rund um die Uhr Menschen arbeiten. Du findest uns auch in der Uni, am Flughafen und im Hotel und überall bieten wir vollwertige Gerichte, Snacks und Getränke genau dort an, wo und wann du sie brauchst.

    Proprietäre Technologien, selbstlernende Algorithmen und effiziente Lieferketten helfen uns, das Paradox zwischen frischem Essen, Verfügbarkeit und Nachhaltigkeit aufzulösen. Durch unsere eigens entwickelte Technologieplattform optimieren wir unsere Mengenplanung und sagen Food Waste den Kampf an. Wir wollen einen positiven Effekt haben - auf die Umwelt, auf den täglichen Alltag unserer Kunden und auf unsere Communities. Deshalb spenden wir Gerichte, die übrig bleiben, an Foodsharing und andere soziale Initiativen direkt vor unserer Haustür.

    Als Marktführer versorgen wir täglich mit Foodji bereits Tausende Menschen deutschlandweit. Zu unseren Kunden zählen unter anderem der Münchner Flughafen, Klarna, Enpal oder Wingcopter. Und wir fangen gerade erst an: allein in Deutschland gibt es mehr als 100.000 relevante Standorte für uns!

Dein Schwerpunkt liegt klar im Bereich Grafik und Gestaltung. Du entwickelst visuelle Ideen und setzt sie für unterschiedliche Projekte und Formate um.

Das ist ausdrücklich nicht der Schwerpunkt deiner Stelle und kein regelmäßiger Bestandteil deines Arbeitsalltags – vielmehr suchen wir jemanden, der ein Teamplayer ist und bei einzelnen Events gerne mal mit anpackt.

Qualifikation

Das bringst du mit

  • ein abgeschlossenes Studium im Bereich Grafikdesign, Kommunikationsdesign oder einer vergleichbaren Fachrichtung
  • idealerweise einen Schwerpunkt oder fundierte Kenntnisse im Bereich Illustration
  • sehr gute Kenntnisse in der Erstellung und Aufbereitung von Druckvorlagen sowie Reinzeichnungen
  • erste Berufserfahrung im Grafik- oder Designbereich ist wünschenswert
  • einen sehr sicheren Umgang mit den gängigen Grafikprogrammen, insbesondere Adobe Illustrator, InDesign und Photoshop
  • ein ausgeprägtes Gespür für Gestaltung, Typografie, Farben und Layout
  • Erfahrung in der Erstellung professioneller Präsentationen
  • eine sorgfältige, strukturierte und selbstständige Arbeitsweise
  • Teamgeist, Zuverlässigkeit und die Bereitschaft, uns gelegentlich auch bei Veranstaltungen vor Ort zu unterstützen

Benefits

Das bieten wir dir

  • Kreative Projekte mit echtem Gestaltungsspielraum: Bei uns geht es nicht nur darum, Vorgaben umzusetzen. Du bist Teil eines Prozesses, in dem aus einer Idee eine Botschaft, ein visuelles Erlebnis und schließlich ein starkes Gesamtergebnis entsteht.
  • Abwechslungsreiche Aufgaben mit viel visueller Konzeption: Besonders spannend wird es dort, wo Inhalte visuell übersetzt werden müssen – zum Beispiel durch Illustrationen, Key Visuals, räumliche Inszenierungen oder die grafische Aufbereitung von Informationen, Zahlen und Daten.
  • Arbeiten an ganzheitlichen Projekten: Unsere Philosophie lautet:
    Konzept → Botschaft → Erlebnis (live und/oder visuell) → Gestaltung → Umsetzung = Erfolg.
    Du arbeitest also nicht isoliert an einzelnen Grafiken, sondern kannst erleben, wie Gestaltung Teil eines gesamten Projekts wird.
  • Nähe zu Events und echten Erlebnissen: Als Eventagentur verbinden wir Gestaltung mit Live-Kommunikation. Dadurch entstehen Projekte, die nicht nur auf dem Bildschirm funktionieren, sondern auch im Raum und vor Ort erlebbar werden.
  • Flexible Arbeitszeitgestaltung unter der Woche: Deine Arbeitszeiten können wir innerhalb der Woche flexibel abstimmen und an deine persönliche Wochenplanung anpassen.
  • Persönliche Zusammenarbeit und kurze Wege: Du arbeitest eng mit unserem Team zusammen und kannst dich direkt in Projekte und kreative Prozesse einbringen.

Noch ein paar Worte zu uns

Wir sind offen für neue Ideen, frische Perspektiven und eigene kreative Ansätze. Wenn du gerne über den Tellerrand schaust, Dinge hinterfragst und eigene Ideen mitbringst, bist du bei uns genau richtig.

Bei uns sollst du nicht einfach nur Aufgaben abarbeiten, sondern dich aktiv einbringen und Gestaltung mitdenken können. Wir freuen uns über Menschen, die Lust haben, Neues auszuprobieren und gemeinsam mit uns Projekte weiterzuentwickeln.

Dich erwartet ein junges, dynamisches und unkompliziertes Team, in dem Zusammenarbeit und gegenseitige Unterstützung großgeschrieben werden.

Und du bist im Grafikbereich nicht auf dich allein gestellt: Eine erfahrene Grafikerin ist bereits Teil unseres Teams und steht dir als Ansprechpartnerin, Unterstützung und fachlicher Leitfaden zur Seite. So gibt es Raum für eigene Ideen und gleichzeitig jemanden, mit dem du dich fachlich jederzeit austauschen kannst.

Wenn du Lust hast, dich kreativ einzubringen, Verantwortung zu übernehmen und gemeinsam mit uns außergewöhnliche Projekte entstehen zu lassen, freuen wir uns darauf, dich kennenzulernen.

description:
palmerhargreaves ist die Agentur für komplexe Themen und Transformationsaufgaben. Aufgaben

Wenn jemand ChatGPT, Perplexity oder Google AI Overviews nach einer Marke fragt, entscheidet sich in der Antwort, ob diese Marke überhaupt vorkommt – und ob das, was dort über sie steht, stimmt. Wir analysieren das für Konzerne: über fünf KI-Systeme, hunderte Fragen, mehrere Messwellen im Jahr. Aus diesen Rohdaten werden Zahlen, auf die wir Empfehlungen und unsere Kunden Entscheidungen stützen.

  • Du arbeitest in unserem Google-Cloud-Stack: BigQuery für die Datenhaltung, Looker Studio für die Dashboards, Cloud Functions für alles, was automatisch laufen soll

title: Lead IT Operations Specialist (m/f/d)
description:
1KOMMA5°

At 1KOMMA5°, we pursue a clear vision: Living on wind and sunlight forever for free. To make this a reality, we are building the energy system of the future with Heartbeat AI. Want to be part of it?

We bring together regional craftsmanship and scalable software: We don't think of solar, batteries, heat pumps, and e-mobility as isolated components, but control them as an intelligent, integrated overall system in our virtual power plant. Directly connected to the electricity market – in real time, fully automated. This way, energy is used when it is available from renewables and particularly cost-effective. By 2030, our goal is to transition 1.5 million households to renewable energies. Over 3,000 people are working towards this every day, at more than 80 locations worldwide, from Finland to Australia.

Want to take responsibility and build solutions that truly matter? Apply now and help us shape the energy world of tomorrow.

Learn about our Product & Tech team!

Deine Position

As the Lead Tech Business Partner, you will be the assigned Tech counterpart for the holding/central employees at 1KOMMA5. This means that every 1KOMMA5 employee in the holding will know their Tech Business Partner by name, and have trust to include them in all technical discussions that improve their productivity. You are accountable for the holdings success.

The average day of a Lead Tech Business Partner

The role is divided into 3 key value areas

  1. Tech Support on level 1, 2 and 3 tickets created by holding employees. The goal here is to be familiar with stakeholders for faster, more efficient turnaround. Tickets are not escalated, but are triaged and discussed to improve technical understanding and develop. You will also monitor queues for the other markets for urgent out of hours requests, and action them when necessary. Level 1 and 2 tickets may be delegated to working students in the team, with guidance and accountability.
  2. Tech Projects - This refers to projects imposed by Employee Technology Platform product strategy such as rollout of Chrome OS and tool consolidations for the holding. This also refers to inbound projects imposed by holding teams (e.g. tailor onboarding experience, setup n8n flows).
  3. Tech Consulting - Providing solutions using existing tools first, through enablement sessions. If no solutions exist, working with teams to technically own and benchmark new applications. There is a particular push to enable AI usage to boost productivity. This means any queries on how to use basic or advanced AI toolings would be directed to this role.

Your stakeholders will be part of your peer review cycle, in which the score will be based on user satisfaction with your support, project and consulting skills. It will also be used to monitor the user base's enablement, to ensure they know the basics of AI, how and where to create tickets etc.

Typical first 90 days - Specific to Lead Tech Business Partnering

  1. Learn processes and take over support tickets for the business unit assigned to. Report on opportunities to optimize to reduce case load.
  2. Proactively meet with all holding team leads, ideally in-person to introduce and explain the value and purpose of Tech Business Partners.
  3. Take over IT onboarding sessions so that all newbies joining the holding know who their Tech Business Partner is from day one.
  4. Take over leadership responsibilities of IC1-IC3 Tech Business Partners assigned to the holding

Dein Profil

  • Minimum of 10+ years of proven professional experience in IT systems, systems engineering or a related field
  • Experience with IT support ticketing best practices, and analysis
  • Proven ability to lead a small and assertive team
  • Proven ability to work both independently, and as part of a team on Technology related projects
  • Profound knowledge of Google Workspace, Office 365, Mobile Device Management (JAMF and InTune) and other SaaS applications (Zoho CRM is a huge plus) surrounding employee productivity, collaboration and security
  • Profound knowledge of AI tooling, specifically relating to employee productivity
  • Understanding on how to utilize scripting to build bespoke functions. Experience with web-front end HTML, CSS, AppScript, Python and Cursor AI
  • Understanding of the workings of cloud infrastructure and code deployment practices and discipline is a huge plus
  • Generalist knowledge of office infrastructure (e.g. office WLAN)
  • Comprehensive knowledge and proven disciplinary action of domain management
  • Strong people skills, being able to persuade and consult non-technical stakeholders on technical solutions
  • Ability to demonstrate methodology
  • Ability to collaborate in a fast-paced, agile environment and adapt to changing priorities while maintaining a security focus
  • Relevant IT Bachelors or Masters degree - certifications related to MTD, MAM are a plus
  • German and English written and verbal communication
  • Willingness to travel primarily to 1KOMMA5 the other holding locations (Munich & Hamburg)

Benefits

  • You are part of an international, dynamic, and highly motivated team of people who have proven to make things happen
  • With your work, you accelerate the "energy transition" and hence have a direct impact on our climate
  • Work with and learn from other super-smart colleagues
  • You will enjoy direct contact with core decision-makers
  • You will enjoy the best chances of entering full-time in one of Europe’s most thriving scaleups
  • You work remotely (Germany-wide), with offices in Hamburg, Berlin or Munich
  • Create a healthy balance alongside your work and enjoy all the benefits of the EGYM Wellpass
  • Benefits and discounts are yours with Futurebens
  • Whether city bike or e-bike - be flexible with our job bike leasing and do something good for the environment at the same time

Als Content Director verantwortest du unser gesamtes Content-Ökosystem. Du produzierst nicht Inhalte, du baust Marken, die ihren Markt dominieren.

Dafür brauchst du keine Einarbeitung in unsere Welt. Du kommst aus dem Personal-Branding-, Creator- oder Agentur-Umfeld, aus Online-Bildung, Coaching oder Consulting, oder du hast selbst Kanäle im Finanz- und Business-Bereich groß gemacht. Du kennst die Zielgruppe, die Plattformlogik und den Unterschied zwischen Reichweite und Umsatz.

Und du willst mehr. Diese Rolle gehört jemandem, der den Anspruch hat, den größten Content-Auftritt seiner Branche zu bauen, und der sich daran messen lassen will. Wer hier auf klare Ansagen wartet, ist falsch.

Ergebnisse, an denen du gemessen wirst

  • Wachstum der Kanäle in Reichweite, Watch-Time und Followern

About Unity Advisory

Unity Advisory is a pure-play, experience-led CFO advisory firm providing integrated finance, commercial, tax and deals support. We are free from audit conflicts and AI-enabled by design, combining deep technical expertise with automation, analytics and AI built into the delivery of every engagement. We are building an alternative to traditional advisory firms, focused on clarity over complexity, outcomes over hours, and practical advice delivered at pace for CFOs making high-consequence decisions.

Unity Advisory is a new kind of partner for the office of the CFO. Founded by senior leaders from the world's top advisory firms and backed by Warburg Pincus, we provide integrated finance, commercial, tax and deals support: expert advice, sharper execution, and delivery models built around how organisations operate today. CFOs need trusted advisers without legacy complexity, so we pair expert human judgement with proprietary AI workflows and smart automation, free from audit conflicts.

The Role

We built our deals practice around the client's decision: whether to buy, whether to sell, at what price, on what terms. We work alongside our clients rather than at arm's length, in the room while the deal decision is being made, and our support carries on beyond signing: into the 100-day plan, the hold period and the eventual exit. And that support draws on the whole firm: our tax, finance and commercial specialists work as one team with the deals practice, so the advice a client gets after signing is as integrated as the diligence that came before it.

We're looking for a Manager to join our Financial Due Diligence team. You'll run buy-side and sell-side engagements day to day: getting into the numbers, managing the team on the ground, and making sure clients get clear, well-supported findings on time.

You'll bring solid FDD or transaction services experience from a Big 4 or top-tier advisory firm, and own an engagement from scoping through to final findings. You'll work alongside our Partners and Directors and directly with clients and target company management from day one. This is a hybrid role based in our Mayfair office.

What You'll Do

• Manage buy-side and sell-side financial due diligence engagements from scoping through to completion.

• Analyse quality of earnings, net working capital, cash flow and other issues that decide a deal, and turn the findings into a clear, well-supported story for the client.

• Run the engagement team day to day: reviewing work, coaching junior staff, and keeping everyone (including the client) up to speed on progress.

• Interview target company management and build working relationships with clients, private equity investors, and other advisors on the deal.

• Draft and quality-check diligence deliverables so they're accurate, clear, and ready for Director or Partner sign-off.

• Work alongside Unity's data and AI specialists to make our analytics standard practice on every engagement.

• Take part in business development: proposals, pitches, and staying close to opportunities as they arise.

What You'll Bring

• 5+ years' experience in Financial Due Diligence or Transaction Services from a Big 4 or top-tier advisory firm.

• Hands-on experience managing buy-side and sell-side FDD assignments from start to finish.

• Strong technical grounding in accounting and the deal issues that matter most: quality of earnings, working capital, and cash flow.

• A track record of being an excellent team player in multidisciplinary engagements.

• Clear and confident communication (both written and verbal) with clients and senior stakeholders.

• Curiosity and genuine interest in how technology and AI evolve financial due diligence practice and playing a key role in shaping it.

• Qualified accountant (ACA, ACCA, CIMA or equivalent).

Nice to Have

• Experience with Private Equity clients or PE-backed portfolio companies.

• Exposure to cross-border or international transactions.

• Experience with data and analytics tools such as Power BI, Alteryx, or Databricks.

• Sector experience in areas like TMT, Consumer, Healthcare, Business Services and Industrials.

title: Technical Product Manager (Superapp)
description:
About Lendable

Lendable is on a mission to build the world's best technology to help people get credit and save money. We're building one of the world’s leading fintech companies and are off to a strong start:

  • One of the UK’s newest unicorns with a team of just over 700 people

  • Among the fastest-growing tech companies in the UK

  • Profitable since 2017

  • Backed by top investors including Balderton Capital and Goldman Sachs

  • Loved by customers with the best reviews in the market (4.9 across 10,000s of reviews on Trustpilot)

So far, we’ve rebuilt the Big Three consumer finance products from scratch: loans, credit cards and car finance. We get money into our customers’ hands in minutes instead of days.

We’re growing fast, and there’s a lot more to do: we’re going after the two biggest Western markets (UK and US) where trillions worth of financial products are held by big banks with dated systems and painful processes.

Join us if you want to

  1. Take ownership across a broad remit. You are trusted to make decisions that drive a material impact on the direction and success of Lendable from day 1

  2. Work in small teams of exceptional people, who are relentlessly resourceful to solve problems and find smarter solutions than the status quo

  3. Build the best technology in-house, using new data sources, machine learning and AI to make machines do the heavy lifting

About the role

We're building a larger, dedicated Platform team at Lendable to reinvest in infrastructure after a deliberate trade-off earlier in the year prioritised new product development. Platform work has been largely invisible to leadership, and without commercial and prioritisation accountability it's been hard to prioritise effectively or connect engineering effort to customer and revenue outcomes.

That's changing. We're hiring a Technical PM to sit within engineering and own the intersection between platform infrastructure and commercial value - not a traditional feature PM, not a people manager and not a project manager: you set priorities, not schedules. The TPM is a commercially accountable IC who owns platform stability and outcomes, embedded in the engineering team.

The core tension you'll resolve: platform engineers make decisions without enough business context; product teams don't always understand what platform work enables or what it costs to defer it. You own both sides of that translation.

This is an IC role with hands-on technical contribution expected, writing code, reviewing PRs, participating in architecture design. That credibility with senior engineers isn't optional; it's how the role works.

You'll partner closely with the Platform Engineering Manager (who owns people and delivery) and the Platform Tech Lead (who owns technical direction and standards). You set what we build and why; they set how the team runs and how it's built. You and the EM are tightly coupled and work from one shared roadmap: you set and sequence priorities, the EM commits capacity and delivery against them.

What you'll be doing

Own platform stability

  • Own platform stability as a primary accountability - SLA/SLO metrics, incident rates, release quality.

  • Hold release gating authority: block features from production that don't meet testing standards or introduce unacceptable regression risk.

  • Enforce CI/CD standards centrally so pods don't fragment into one-off solutions.

  • Track and report stability metrics alongside commercial outcomes - stability is the foundation that makes the rest possible.

Be commercially accountable

  • Own the business case for platform investment and answer "why are we spending six engineers on this for three months?" in terms leadership understands.

  • Track platform impact in business terms: developer velocity, incident cost, time-to-market, reliability, capacity - e.g. "CXO rollout removes a 3-second API fan-out, reducing session abandonment" or "we can now handle 20k simultaneous logins".

  • Input into headcount and investment decisions for the platform team.

Own the platform roadmap

  • Own the platform backlog, prioritised by business value and sequenced to unblock the highest-value product teams first - not driven by technical debt or engineer preference alone.

  • Make trade-offs explicit: "if we do X now, we defer Y by Z weeks - here's what that means for products depending on us".

  • Ensure every initiative has a defined success metric that non-engineers can track.

Be the stakeholder interface

  • Act as the single point of contact for Pod Leads: business requirements coming from pods and engineering/developer requirements flowing to pods; prioritise both in service of platform stability.

  • Make platform work visible to leadership - regular forums with product MDs and PMs to capture upcoming dependencies before they become blockers; represent platform work in leadership reviews; translate technical milestones into business milestones.

  • Drive cross-team collaboration and buy-in with other PMs; engage architecture in technical design.

  • Escalate when product teams make requests that would create unsustainable platform load or technical debt.

description:
About Odin

Odin is building the investment infrastructure for the future of private markets.
We believe capital is one of the most powerful tools for shaping the world - and more people should be putting it to work. Our mission is to make it radically easier to raise and deploy capital, so that anyone, anywhere, can back the companies and ideas they believe in.

Our first product is a full-stack platform for launching and running private investment firms - think Shopify for VC and PE. We handle all the infrastructure: from legals and investor onboarding to KYC/AML, payments, tax, reporting, and exits.

We’re already trusted by over 10,000 angels, VCs, and founders. We administer over $500m in assets, covering investments from pre-seed to series E. This includes household names like ElevenLabs, OpenAI, SpaceX, xAI, Anduril, etc. but also new companies creating everything from synthetic brains to small nuclear reactors.

Why We’re Hiring

Our Investor Experience at Odin is how we win.

Our customers come to us at the highest-stakes moments of their professional lives. They’re closing deals, calling capital, moving real money, and dealing with real regulators. When something breaks or feels uncertain, you are the person they turn to. You are the face of Odin in those moments.

Your job is not to close tickets. Your job is to make sure customers love Odin so much they tell other people about us and make every future customer’s experience better than the last.

Responsibilities

  • Own the end-to-end experience for our customers (angels, VCs, GPs, LPs and founders) across the full deal lifecycle: pre-close, closing, post-close and ongoing reporting.

  • Be the primary respondent on inbound questions, with the authority and judgement to move deals forward and resolve hard cases without escalation.

  • Triage with judgement: spot what’s urgent, what’s risky (money or compliance), what can be self-served and what genuinely needs Product, Ops or Compliance, and route accordingly.

  • Reduce ticket volume by going to the root cause. Identify the patterns and feed back to Product with clarity and conviction. The goal is fewer tickets next quarter than this one.

  • Be the internal voice of the customer. When something keeps coming up, you don’t just log it, you advocate for it until it’s fixed, and then you go back to the customer and close the loop.

  • Set the tone and standards for how Odin shows up to customers. Document what good looks like. Help the team raise the bar.

Who You Are

  • You take real pride in how you come across. You see communication & relationship-building as a craft.

  • You have at least 5 years of experience in a relationship-driven role. Direct experience in VC, private equity, finance, or a regulated environment is a strong plus.

  • You’re calm and clear under pressure. When customers are stressed and money is on the line, you meet them where they are: confident, peer-level, no apology theatre, no fluff.

  • When something is painful or repetitive, your instinct is to fix the root cause, not to power through it.

  • You have high conviction. You’ll push back, you’ll challenge, and you’ll back down when you’re wrong. You’d rather be useful than be liked.

  • You’re a high-ownership, low-ego team player. You leave ego at the door, you default to “we”, and you raise the bar through how you show up day-to-day.

  • You can write really well. Tone matters. Our customers are sophisticated, busy and pay close attention.

  • You want a startup, not a corporate. You can articulate why: high ownership, fast-moving, ambiguous, real impact, real growth, no waiting for permission.

Working at Odin

title: Client Director
description:
MISSION

Bei STAN sind Client Directors strategische Sparringspartner – keine klassischen Account Manager. Sie führen anspruchsvolle Kundenbeziehungen auf höchstem Niveau, gestalten strategische Diskussionen, erkennen Chancen, bevor sie entstehen, und stellen sicher, dass jede Zusammenarbeit die Qualität, den Anspruch und die Denkweise widerspiegelt, für die STAN steht. Sie übernehmen die ganzheitliche Verantwortung für den Erfolg ihrer Kunden und tragen gleichzeitig aktiv zu Strategie, Wachstum und exzellenter kreativer Arbeit bei.


DEINE AUFGABEN

Client Leadership & Strategische Partnerschaft

  • Werde vertrauensvoller Sparringspartner für unsere Kunden und baue Beziehungen auf, die weit über einzelne Projekte hinausgehen.
  • Übernimm die vollständige Verantwortung für den Erfolg, die Entwicklung und das Wachstum deines Kundenportfolios und stelle sicher, dass kein Detail verloren geht und jede Zusammenarbeit außergewöhnlichen Mehrwert schafft.
  • Erkenne Kundenbedürfnisse, geschäftliche Herausforderungen und neue Chancen, bevor sie von deinen Kunden selbst identifiziert werden.
  • Berate CEOs, Gründer:innen, CMOs und weitere Führungskräfte souverän zu Themen wie Unternehmensstrategie, Markenentwicklung, kultureller Relevanz, Innovation, Partnerschaften und Wachstum.
  • Führe strategische Gespräche, moderiere Workshops und begleite komplexe Stakeholder-Prozesse mit Klarheit, Souveränität und Überzeugungskraft.

Strategische Beratung

  • Entwickle strategische Narrative, Positionierungen, kulturelle Plattformen und Wachstumsstrategien mit nachhaltiger Wirkung.
  • Übersetze komplexe unternehmerische Herausforderungen in klare strategische Empfehlungen und umsetzbare Lösungen.
  • Erarbeite Strategien, schärfe Botschaften, optimiere Präsentationen und hinterfrage Denkansätze, um jede Arbeit auf das nächste Niveau zu heben.
  • Arbeite eng mit den STAN Foundern sowie den Teams aus New Business, Strategy, Creative, Production, Social und AI zusammen, um strategisches Denken in außergewöhnliche Umsetzung zu übersetzen.
  • Verbinde Ideen, Branchen und Chancen auf unerwartete Weise und schaffe dadurch strategische Wettbewerbsvorteile für unsere Kunden.

Kundenerfolg & Qualität

  • Übernimm die Gesamtverantwortung für die Kundenbeziehung – von der strategischen Ausrichtung bis zur finalen Umsetzung.
  • Fungiere als Qualitätsinstanz für sämtliche Kundenprojekte und stelle sicher, dass jede Arbeit den kreativen Ansprüchen von STAN entspricht.
  • Hinterfrage Ideen kontinuierlich, schärfe Ergebnisse und hebe gemeinsam mit den Teams das strategische und kreative Niveau.
  • Sorge dafür, dass Projekte mit höchster Qualität, Konsistenz und Liebe zum Detail umgesetzt werden.

Wachstum & Geschäftsentwicklung

  • Erkenne Potenziale, bestehende Kundenbeziehungen durch neue Projekte, strategische Partnerschaften und langfristige Retainer auszubauen.
  • Entwickle Angebote, Leistungsumfänge und strategische Empfehlungen, die sowohl für unsere Kunden als auch für STAN nachhaltigen Mehrwert schaffen.
  • Baue vertrauensvolle Beziehungen auf, aus denen langfristige Partnerschaften, Folgeprojekte und Weiterempfehlungen entstehen.

Beziehungsentwicklung

  • Entwickle langfristige Partnerschaften, die auf Vertrauen, Glaubwürdigkeit und exzellentem Service basieren.
  • Erkenne Potenziale, bestehende Kundenbeziehungen weiterzuentwickeln und nachhaltige Kooperationen aufzubauen.
  • Werde durch proaktives Denken, Verlässlichkeit und strategische Führung zu einem geschätzten Teil der Teams unserer Kunden.
  • Repräsentiere STAN souverän in Kundenterminen, Workshops, internationalen Präsentationen und Branchenevents.

Leadership

  • Führe interdisziplinäre Teams mit Empathie, Klarheit und hohen Qualitätsansprüchen.
  • Inspiriere und fördere Kolleg:innen und schaffe ein Umfeld, in dem außergewöhnliche Arbeit entstehen kann.
  • Übernimm Verantwortung statt lediglich zu koordinieren – indem du mit gutem Beispiel vorangehst und selbst aktiv zu strategischen und kreativen Ergebnissen beiträgst.


DEIN PROFIL

Strategische Führungspersönlichkeit

  • Mindestens 6-8 Jahre Berufserfahrung in einer führenden Kreativagentur, Markenberatung oder Strategieberatung.
  • Umfangreiche Erfahrung in der Führung internationaler Kunden sowie komplexer Stakeholder-Strukturen.
  • Fundiertes Verständnis von Unternehmensstrategie, Markenentwicklung, Cultural Strategy, Innovation, Experience Design und integrierter Kommunikation.
  • Nachweisbare Erfahrung darin, strategische Empfehlungen zu entwickeln und überzeugend vor Führungskräften und Entscheidungsträgern zu präsentieren.

Hands-on-Berater:in

  • Du koordinierst nicht nur Spezialisten, sondern arbeitest selbst aktiv an den Inhalten mit.
  • Du entwickelst Strategien, optimierst Präsentationen, moderierst Workshops, schärfst Botschaften und hinterfragst Denkansätze.
  • Du verbindest strategische Exzellenz mit unternehmerischem Verständnis und einer außergewöhnlich hohen Umsetzungsqualität.
  • Du erkennst Chancen frühzeitig, löst Probleme proaktiv und bringst Projekte mit Eigeninitiative voran.

Beziehungsmanager:in

  • Du baust Vertrauen auf, bevor es um Geschäft geht.
  • Du entwickelst langfristige Partnerschaften, anstatt Projekte lediglich zu verwalten.
  • Du verstehst es, Kunden zu inspirieren, herauszufordern und zu überzeugen, ohne tragfähige Beziehungen zu gefährden.
  • Du überzeugst durch Souveränität, Präsenz und ein sicheres Urteilsvermögen auf Executive-Ebene.

Unternehmerisches Denken

  • Du erkennst Potenziale, Kundenbeziehungen durch strategisches Denken und vertrauensvolle Partnerschaften nachhaltig weiterzuentwickeln.
  • Du fühlst dich sicher im Umgang mit Angeboten, Leistungsumfängen und langfristigen Zusammenarbeitsmodellen.
  • Du verstehst, wie exzellente Kundenführung nachhaltiges Unternehmenswachstum ermöglicht.

Qualitätsanspruch

  • Du verfügst über ein außergewöhnliches Gespür für Qualität und höchste Ansprüche an jedes Detail.
  • Du hebst die Qualität jeder Arbeit und inspirierst dein Umfeld dazu, denselben Anspruch zu verfolgen.
  • Dir sind kreative Exzellenz und messbarer geschäftlicher Erfolg gleichermaßen wichtig.

Persönliche Eigenschaften

  • Neugierig, unternehmerisch denkend und von Natur aus proaktiv.
  • Ruhig und souverän – auch in dynamischen oder unklaren Situationen.
  • Begeistert für Kultur, Kreativität, KI, Innovation und die Zukunft von Marken und Unternehmen.
  • Hervorragende Englischkenntnisse in Wort und Schrift (nahezu muttersprachliches Niveau) sind Voraussetzung. Weitere Sprachkenntnisse wie Deutsch, Französisch oder Arabisch sind von Vorteil.
  • Erfahrung oder Interesse im Bereich Women's Health ist von Vorteil.

Verfügbarkeit

  • Wohnsitz in den USA, idealerweise in New York oder Los Angeles.
  • Die Zusammenarbeit startet zunächst auf Freelance-Basis mit der Perspektive, diese langfristig in eine Festanstellung zu überführen.
